subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Should this issue require current-main live Twilio/OpenAI audio proof before any close or fix, and which boundary should own the eventual change if clipping reproduces?
rationale: Source inspection shows plausible mitigations already on main, but only live carrier audio evidence can distinguish fixed behavior from a remaining provider, codec, gain, or pacing bug.

options.title: Require live audio diagnosis
options.body: Keep this open until a maintainer or reporter provides redacted current-main call audio/log proof that identifies the failing layer before changing code.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow experiment
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly choose a codec/gain or pacing experiment without full proof, accepting the risk to all realtime call audio.

options.title: Close with private proof
options.body: Close only if maintainers already have current-main live proof that the clipping no longer occurs and can summarize the evidence publicly.

recommendation.title: Require live audio diagnosis
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a maintainer or reporter provides redacted current-main call audio/log proof that identifies the failing layer before changing code.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans shared audio codec behavior and recent voice-call proof standards, and this owner has the clearest recent codec history in the affected shared path.
